A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same discrete Schrödinger-bridge benchmark and solver framework. All 21 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable; relocated propositions, tables and figures can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original numerical and visual evaluations of CSBM, α-CSBM, DLightSB and DLightSB-M on synthetic Gaussian-mixture benchmarks, including Tables 1–4 and Figures 1–5.

after.justification: V2 reports original solver evaluations, additional baseline comparisons, trajectory-KL measurements and a reverse-direction experiment in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The CP-based benchmark construction and the three proposed solvers retain their procedures and objectives. V2 expands explanations of sampling, normalization and dimension-wise losses. Its Proposition 3.2 largely relocates transition mathematics already present in v1 Proposition 4.3 and Appendix A; this does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: V2 adds reverse-direction transport evaluation using the existing benchmark marginals, changing the conditional generation task (Appendix D.1). The principal coverage remains synthetic Gaussian-mixture problems with 50 categories, dimensions 2, 16 and 64, and Gaussian or uniform reference processes.

E2.justification: V2 adds three evaluated comparators absent from v1's result tables: Independent, Reference and Feature-wise SB. They appear alongside the retained solvers in conditional and unconditional comparisons; Reference and Feature-wise SB also enter the new trajectory-KL comparisons. These substantially expand the evaluation's diagnostic controls.

E3.justification: V2 introduces forward and reverse trajectory-KL evaluation and a classifier-based ROC-AUC protocol for reverse transport. The stated conditional evaluation changes from 156 source points in v1 Appendix C to 157 in v2 Section 5.2, retaining 1,000 outputs per point. The principal training budgets and 20,000-pair test set remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The new reverse benchmark tests whether DLightSB's advantage depends on alignment with the benchmark's CP construction (Appendix D.1, Table 2). Additional baseline comparisons diagnose the distinction between conditional and unconditional fidelity (Tables 1, 5 and 6). These extend the earlier loss-function and timestep comparisons to central questions about benchmark validity.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance testing for the experiments. V2 uses C2ST as a point-valued ROC-AUC metric, without introducing uncertainty estimates or hypothesis-test significance reporting.

E6.justification: Conditional and unconditional scores are extensively revised, and baseline, C2ST and trajectory-KL results are added. For example, DLightSB's conditional Shape/Trend scores at D=16 with Gaussian reference γ=0.02 change from 0.972/0.943 in v1 Tables 1–2 to 0.85/0.76 in v2 Table 1. These are reported-value changes, not established same-protocol performance losses, given the revised evaluation description.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the circular definition of the SB set in v1 Equations 19–20, replacing it with Equation 18. Theorem 3.1's proof receives corrected algebra, explicit normalization and a strict-convexity argument. It also adds a trajectory-KL decomposition assertion. The principal benchmark and optimal-projection results remain; the transition proposition is substantially inherited from v1.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a ground-truth benchmark for discrete SB/EOT, the same three adapted solvers, and evaluation in high-dimensional discrete settings. V2 foregrounds computational tractability and the shortage of solvers, but these elaborate existing contributions rather than introduce different core claims.

C2.justification: V1 attributes DLightSB's advantage to alignment with the benchmark; v2 explicitly treats it as oracle-like and less informative about general solver performance. The explanation for DLightSB-M's deficit changes from iterative sampling error to loss-estimation variance. V2 also adds baseline-failure and reverse-test interpretations, including an inconsistent claim that near-one C2ST ROC-AUC indicates inability to distinguish samples.

D1.justification: V2 supplies an explicit catsbench repository link instead of only referring to supplementary code. It specifies Gaussian-core means on a radius-5 sphere, dimension-dependent standard deviations, independent initialization for the CSBM variants, and the C2ST classifier architecture. Most optimizer, training-budget and hardware details persist, while some explicit log-parameter optimization and memory-scaling details from v1 Appendix B disappear.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting earlier OT benchmarks, Markov-chain embeddability, SB transitions, IMF convergence rates and C2ST, including Korotin et al. (2021; 2022), Kingman (1962) and Lopez-Paz and Oquab (2017). The central positioning as a discrete counterpart to continuous-space work remains. Kholkin and Peluchetti publication updates concern existing cited works.

P1.justification: The introduction, background, benchmark construction and solver explanations undergo extensive rewriting and reorganization. Transition parameterization moves into Section 3.2, the uniform-reference derivation moves into Appendix B, and Appendix D gains separate reverse-benchmark and additional-results sections. These are substantial narrative changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V1's two conditional-score tables become side-by-side panels of v2 Table 1, with additional baseline rows and revised color thresholds. V2 adds C2ST and two trajectory-KL tables and reformats the unconditional tables. Figures 1–5 retain the same underlying images but are relocated and reflowed; the substantial new visual content is in the tables.

improvement.justification: V2 improves baseline coverage, reproducibility information and several mathematical explanations and definitions. However, Appendix D.1 interprets ROC-AUC values of 0.90–1.00 as inability to distinguish samples, and Section 5.1 does not justify equating summed coordinate-marginal divergences with full trajectory KL for dependent CP transitions. These unresolved problems affect the new validation central to the benchmark, preventing a reliable judgment that the benefits outweigh the harms.
